title: Автограф для военкомата  (An Autograph for the Draft Board)

segments.t: Remembering Aleksandr's boast about dodging the army, Max devises the ultimate payback. He tells Aleksandr that an admirer in the dining room wants his autograph, leading the vain chef straight to a military draft officer who tricks him into signing his own conscription summons.
Надо тебя завтра в дворники понизить.
Хотел бы вас с автограф попросить.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Aleksandr Sergeyevich, the guests are calling for you.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'Alexander', while 'call' completes the thought.
'They want to get your autograph.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'want' before landing on 'autograph'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Oh, super.' The grammar packs 'about' and 'super' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'How are things going in your new position?' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'how' and 'on' in a few short words.
'I am managing. Well, well.' Notice how Russian expresses 'cope' and 'yeah' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Lyova answers right away.
Надо тебя завтра в дворники понизить.
'I ought to demote you to janitor tomorrow.' In Russian, the idea of 'at' flows naturally into 'demote' without extra filler words.
Хотел бы вас с автограф попросить.
'I would like to ask you for an autograph.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'wanted' and 'would' in a few short words.
'Good evening.' Lyova anchors the line on 'good', while 'evening' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Do you have a pen on you?' Russian expresses 'having' with the preposition 'by' plus the genitive pronoun and 'you'.
'Yes, of course.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'yes' before landing on 'of course'.
'Right here, please.' The grammar packs 'there you go' and 'here' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Lyova answers right away.
'Could you write at the top who it is for?' The grammar packs 'can' and 'whom' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.

'It is time to pay your debt to the Motherland.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'it is time' and 'motherland' in a few short words. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
Надо тебя завтра в дворники понизить.
Хотел бы вас с автограф попросить.
